t: None of the funds appropriated or otherwise made available under this Act shall be obligated or expended in connection with any base realignment or closure activity, until all terms, conditions and requirements of the National Environmental Policy Act have been complied with, with respect to each such activity.

fable.w: This is an appropriations restriction that bars spending on base realignment or closure until NEPA has been complied with. The tempting reading is that NEPA's environmental review process usually involves public comment, so the cross-reference imports participation. But the section itself names no outside party, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue; it only conditions funding on compliance with another statute. That makes it a funding limitation rather than a participation requirement.
fable.s: until all terms, conditions and requirements of the National Environmental Policy Act have been complied with

opus.w: The section bars spending on any base realignment or closure until NEPA's requirements are fully met. Those requirements include public scoping, public comment on environmental reviews, and consultation with states, tribes and local governments. That puts outside participation in front of each federal closure decision. Reading it as a pure spending limit misses that the condition is itself a process involving the public, though the participation is only incorporated by reference.
opus.s: until all terms, conditions and requirements of the National Environmental Policy Act have been complied with, with respect to each such activity
opus.b:
I'm labelling this **Yes**, but with low confidence.

The tempting reading is that this is only a limit on spending. It names no outside party and no hearing or comment period, and nothing in the text itself crosses the federal boundary. That reading misses what the section actually conditions the money on. Funds can't be spent on base closures until "all terms, conditions and requirements" of the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) are met. Relying on ordinary legal background, NEPA's requirements include public scoping and comment periods on environmental reviews, and consultation with states, tribes and local governments. So the section brings that outside participation in before each federal decision. Confidence is low because outsiders are only reached through the reference to NEPA; the section never mentions them directly.

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes a condition on the expenditure of funds, requiring compliance with the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA). While NEPA often involves public participation, this specific section does not explicitly mandate any participatory process (such as public comments, hearings, or consultation with outside entities) itself. It merely references compliance with another statute as a prerequisite for spending. Therefore, the section itself does not describe or require participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: None of the funds appropriated or otherwise made available under this Act shall be obligated or expended in connection with any base realignment or closure activity, until all terms, conditions and requirements of the National Environmental Policy Act have been complied with, with respect to each such activity.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) inherently requires public participation (e.g., public comment periods for Environmental Impact Statements), so referencing NEPA compliance implies participation. However, the section itself does not explicitly mandate any specific participatory process; it merely sets a condition for the expenditure of funds based on compliance with another statute. The definition requires the section itself to involve participation (consultation, hearings, advisory boards with outsiders, etc.). Since this section is a funding restriction contingent on external legal compliance, and does not describe the participatory mechanisms itself, it is not a direct instance of participation as defined. Furthermore, NEPA compliance can sometimes be satisfied through categorical exclusions or other means that might not involve direct public participation in every instance, though typically it does. But strictly speaking, the text here is about fund obligation conditions, not the participatory act itself. More importantly, the definition says "Participation is when the federal government may or must consult or coordinate with people outside of the government...". This section doesn't say the government must consult; it says funds can't be spent until NEPA is complied with. While NEPA often involves participation, this specific text is a fiscal constraint. However, looking at the "No" traps: "reports to... Congress", "consultation... between federal agencies", "applications...". This doesn't fit those. But does it fit "Yes"? "requiring a public comment period, or requiring rulemaking". NEPA often requires an EIS which has a comment period. But does *this section* require it? It requires NEPA compliance. Is that enough? The definition says "Answer 'Yes' when the SECTION involves ANY of the following: ... requiring rulemaking". NEPA isn't rulemaking per se, it's environmental review. The section doesn't explicitly mention public comment, hearings, or advisory committees. It just cites NEPA. Given the strict instruction to check WHO is involved and that the text must support the label, and the text here is purely about fund restriction based on a separate act's requirements, it is safer to label "No" because the section itself does not describe the participation mechanism. The participation is in NEPA, not in this section. This section is a "No" because it is a funding restriction, not a participatory provision.
